catalog_quote: 5.10 Stress usually occurs in JB either on the ultimate or the penultimate syllable; in some words, however, stress will occur on the antepenultimate syllable. 5.11 Ultimate stress In words containing more than one syllable, stress will occur on the final syllable - if this contains a long vowel or ends with a cluster: dolmeé "darkness", maswag "a little while", patin "boots", yumén "two days", 'aférr "I'll throw", 'aswddd "I'll become black". ... 5.12 Penultimate stress If the last syllable does not contain a long vowel or does not end in a cluster, then the stress will fall on the penultimate, whether the vowel in the penultimate is long or short: zullyyi "carpet", skdmli "chair", bazziina "cat", gabbitu "his room", 'aftdéham "1'll understand". 5.13 Antepenultimate stress In some words, stress is on the antepenultimate. audit.quote_check: confirmed in the copy we hold
audit.reasoning: Quote check: the deciding passage (Mansour 1991 ch. 5, secs. 5.10-5.13) is present verbatim in the held archive.org scanned text at the stated pages (87-91), and the image PDF we hold visually confirms p. 89 (Blanc discussion, 5.132) word for word; the exceptions quote and the domain footnote are also there. Deciding source: a 1991 reference grammar (xxi+329 pp.) with a dedicated, argued word-stress chapter by a native-speaker scholar - the strongest kind of source short of an instrumental study, and none of the latter is known for JB. Glottolog's list contains only one newer description of this languoid, Bar-Moshe 2019 (Harrassowitz; phonology chapter 14 pp.), which is paywalled (checked publisher page and JSTOR DOI); the same author's 2024 OA textbook, already held, gives the Blanc-type formulation (rightmost long vowel or pre-cluster vowel, else first syllable, plus morphological suffix rule

sources.note: Only post-1991 reference grammar of this languoid; its stress section would show whether the modern description keeps Mansour's 'final-if-heavy else penult' or Blanc's 'rightmost heavy else initial' default (his 2024 textbook, held, uses the latter) and would let the the primary-stress rule note the competing analysis with a primary citation.
